annotations.text:
Nine screens became eight.

The old screen 2 (connector, auth open) and screen 5 (action, Auth) had the same purpose — and the action one was worse than redundant: its entire content was "it's over there". That is the signpost tab I removed from the connector earlier in the session and then rebuilt one level down.

So: a connector is Name, Description, Tags and its Actions — identity and contents, nothing else. Base URL and auth move to the action's Auth tab, where they are actually used, and are editable there.

Screen 4 is the collapse.

Editable, because this is where you are when you need it. Marked shared, because it is: Meta keeps base_url and auth_config on the connector and a tool cannot carry a credential of its own, so one edit changes every action under it. The amber line says so before you type, not after.

The In column — Header / Query / Body — is the gap that stops an ?api_key= API being configurable at all today.

A connector has no tabs and now barely has a screen: three identity rows and the Actions table.

Screen 2 is one with nothing in it — no empty-state message, no Add button. The last row of the table is the affordance, and Publish is greyed because a connector with no actions cannot usefully be published.

One tab row, ever, and it lives inside an action.

Response is pinned to the foot of the pane on EVERY action screen — a 44px "Not sent yet" strip until you Send, then 268px with the status line and the body. It does not move between tabs.

Every table is the same five columns: Key · Type · Source · Description · Required.

The founder's own API: 13 fields under one `detail` object.

day, month, year, lat and lon are required by the API and every one shows a dash — Meta records required-ness only for TOP-LEVEL body fields, and the only top-level field here is `detail`. So the description carries the range, the unit and the word required. There is no min, max or pattern either.

The response is 200 OK with status:failed. A green tick on the status line would report success on a failed call, so the pane shows the body and the strip says read status, not the code.
